an order placed before the cut-off dispatches the same day
an order placed after the cut-off dispatches the next day
promise date = dispatch date + that warehouse’s transit days to that zone
a promise date is never earlier than the dispatch date
no promise date is stored anywhere — it is worked out on every read
an order no warehouse can serve has no promise date at all
changing the warehouse changes the date the customer is given
left alone, an order is served from the fastest warehouse that holds it
allocating by hand overrides the automatic choice
an order cannot be allocated to a warehouse without the stock
nothing can be shipped before it is allocated
every order already past Allocated has a warehouse against it
allocating takes the stock out of that warehouse and no other
cancelling an allocated order puts the stock back where it came from
a backorder is exactly an order nothing can serve
every backorder is raised as urgent
stock everywhere = the sum of the warehouses
stock cannot be moved into the warehouse it came out of
stock cannot be moved out of a warehouse that does not have it
moving stock changes two warehouses and leaves the total alone
on-time counts only orders that actually landed
an order is on time when it landed on or before the date promised
an order that landed after its promise is counted as late
on-time % is the share of landed orders that met their promise
a blown promise is an unshipped order whose date has gone
an order already shipped is never called a blown promise
a refund is impossible before the parcel is back
a refund is impossible before somebody has looked at it
nothing is refunded twice
a resaleable return refunds the whole amount
a damaged return refunds only 50% of the value
a resaleable piece goes back into stock and a damaged one does not
money owed = every return that has not been refunded yet
a parcel booked in is no longer counted as coming back
a parcel already looked at is not on the inspection list
a refused delivery is treated as a return, never as a delivery
every capability this app uses is a known one
no capability offers only one choice
every capability works with nothing connected (built-in or by hand)
every capability has an option you can host yourself
exactly one provider is active per capability
the default provider never needs an outside service
no single company is unavoidable across capabilities
switching a provider changes which one is active
switching a provider changes nothing else in your data

a line naming a ledger is read as a ledger
a line naming a bill is read as a bill
saying print means print
not saying how means send it to me
a document number is picked out of the sentence
"2 copies" is read as two
no number of copies means one
copies are capped, so a typo cannot print a ream
every kind it knows has at least one word that finds it
no two kinds share a word
every registered person has a number and something they may do
no two people share a number
an unregistered number is refused whatever it asks
an unregistered number is refused even for something harmless
a refusal for an unknown number says nothing about what exists
somebody who may only print cannot send a document out
somebody limited to certain documents cannot ask for the others
nothing that moves money can be asked for by anybody
a money word is refused as a shape, not as a permission
the owner is refused exactly like everybody else
sending a document out always waits for a one-time code
printing inside the office never needs a code
a waiting request has a six-digit code
a request is only ever sent after its code is confirmed
every printer says where it is and what it is good for
the default printer is one that is switched on
nothing is queued at a printer that is switched off
every source says what is in it
a ledger is worked out fresh, never hunted for
a scanned document is found, never invented
every kind of document has a source that exists
asking for a filed document that is not there returns nothing rather than something else
every request is on the record, including the refused ones
a refusal always carries its reason
a refused request never produced a document
every request number ever issued still has a row — nothing was removed
this app adds no action that removes a line from the record
every request has a number, and no two share one
how long each answer took is recorded
a document made from the books answers faster than one fetched from storage

spend shares sum to ~100%
risk is bounded 0..100
a late + overdue vendor scores higher risk than a clean one
preferred vendor is the highest-scoring rated one
paying a bill reduces total payable by exactly that amount
